blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Inventory management in practice is a constant game of small adjustments. Nothing is ever perfect. Demand jumps, suppliers slip, and new products arrive while old ones linger. The job is to notice, adjust and move on — repeated every week, across hundreds or thousands of SKUs.

Mature teams use ABC analysis to focus their attention. A items — the biggest 20% that generate 80% of the value — get watched daily. B items get weekly attention. C items get monthly reviews and simple automatic rules.

If the biggest items are right, the rest of the operation has room to breathe. If they are wrong, nothing else can compensate. That is why the best inventory managers spend most of their time on the smallest number of SKUs — and it is why, over a year, they usually outperform teams that try to watch everything at once.

items.q: According to the text, how often are A items reviewed?
items.why: "A items… get watched daily." São os itens mais importantes, revisados todos os dias.

items.q: What is the central idea behind ABC analysis in the text?
options: Automatic rules should manage all items
Every SKU should get the same amount of attention
New products matter more than old ones
Focus attention where most of the value is concentrated
items.why: A tese é focar nos poucos itens (os A) que geram a maior parte do valor.

items.q: The phrase "nothing else can compensate" suggests that…
options: the C items are the most profitable
getting the A items wrong cannot be fixed by managing the others well
teams should ignore the biggest items
items.why: Inferência: se os itens maiores estão errados, acertar os demais não repara o estrago.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: ABC analysis helps managers set priorities
A small set of SKUs deserves most of a manager's attention
Inventory work is a routine of constant small adjustments
Watching every SKU equally is the mark of a strong team
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta contra tentar vigiar tudo igualmente — isso é o que faz times perderem desempenho.

items.q: Why do the best managers usually outperform others over a year?
options: They review all SKUs on the same schedule
They concentrate effort on the fewest, highest-value SKUs
They never let old products linger
They automate every category of stock
items.why: "they usually outperform teams that try to watch everything at once" — a vantagem vem do foco no pequeno número de SKUs de maior valor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry treinando a nova analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before you open that spreadsheet, let me save you a lot of wasted time. You've got about eight hundred SKUs in this warehouse, and I can already see you're planning to check all of them every morning. Don't. You'll be exhausted by Wednesday and you still won't spot the problems that matter.

Here's how I want you to work. Pull the ABC list first. Your A items — maybe forty of them — those you know by name, not by number. If stock on an A item falls below the safety level, the system will flag it, but I want you looking before the system does. The B items you check once a week. The C items? Set a simple reorder rule and leave them alone.

Last quarter the analyst before you spent half her day tidying C items and missed a stockout on one of our top sellers. That single gap cost us more than every C adjustment she made all month. So if you focus on the top twenty percent, the rest will look after itself — and you'll actually go home on time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the new analyst planning to do that Harry tells her not to?
options: Check all the SKUs every morning
items.why: "you're planning to check all of them every morning. Don't."

items.q: How does Harry want her to know the A items?
options: By name, not just by number
items.why: "Your A items… those you know by name, not by number."

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says he wants her "looking before the system does"?
options: The system is unreliable and should be ignored
She should turn off the automatic alerts
She should anticipate problems rather than only react to alerts
She should check the system twice a day
items.why: Inferência: bom gestor previne — ele quer que ela perceba a queda antes de o sistema disparar o alerta.

items.q: Why does Harry mention the previous analyst?
options: To praise how tidy the C items were kept
To explain why the safety level was raised
To show that C items deserve most of the attention
To warn that misplaced focus caused a costly stockout on a top seller
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo ilustra o custo de gastar tempo com C e descuidar de um item A.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's overall message?
options: Work harder and check more items each day
Treat every category with equal care
Focus effort on the few items that matter most
Trust the system and stop reviewing stock
items.why: "if you focus on the top twenty percent, the rest will look after itself" — foco, não esforço espalhado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The supplier said the shipment would slip by three days." Here, to slip means to…
items.why: To slip = atrasar; o prazo escorregou para depois.

items.q: "A few discontinued products still linger on the shelves." To linger means to…
items.why: To linger = permanecer, ficar parado por mais tempo do que se esperava.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Getting the A items right means the C items barely need any ___."
items.why: Adjustment = ajuste; os itens C exigem poucos ajustes quando os A estão sob controle.

items.q: "Careful A-item management helps the team outperform its rivals." To outperform means to…
items.why: To outperform = superar, ter desempenho melhor do que.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "With over a thousand ___ to track, no one can review every single line by hand."
items.why: SKU = a unidade de controle de estoque; são elas que se contam aos milhares no armazém.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de operações e estoque. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The system will trigger a reorder when stock hits the safety level." To trigger a reorder means to…
options: automatically start a new purchase order
items.why: Trigger a reorder = disparar/acionar automaticamente um novo pedido de reposição.

items.q: "Overstocking C items ties up cash we need elsewhere." To tie up cash means to…
options: delay a payment to a supplier
keep money locked in something unproductive
items.why: Tie up cash = imobilizar dinheiro, deixá-lo preso em estoque parado.

items.q: "We missed a demand spike and ran out of our top seller." To run out of means to…
items.why: Run out of = ficar sem, esgotar o estoque de algo.

items.q: "Once the rules are set, the C items pretty much look after themselves." This means they…
items.why: Look after themselves = se cuidam sozinhos, quase não pedem intervenção.

items.q: "Tidying C items all day will not move the needle on service levels." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível — aqui, não causa.
